Maya (eng-runtime): follow-up on yesterday's design chat: can we commit to a much smaller operator surface for dedicated pools? goal: safer upgrades + clear cost controls.
Dan (orch): what small means to me: operator manages node state + token validation only. admission logic lives in a proxy service.
Lea (sre): +1 for smaller surface. fewer CRDs reduces blast radius. need strong metrics though: pool_util, queued_tokens, fallback_count.
Omar (product): product needs deterministic behavior per tier. propose lane configs (concurrency, prewarm, fallback-model) served from config-service.
Maya (eng-runtime): admission proto sketch: POST /admit {tenant, lane, want_slots, trace_id} -> {granted, ttl, fallback_hint}. simple and auditable.
Dan (orch): reconciler scope: only pool geometry and node labels. autoscaler consumes token-pressure + util metrics to decide scale. no intent APIs.
Lea (sre): for burst credits, keep accounting in billing service. admission fetches ephemeral slices; on conflict billing handles optimistic decrements.
Omar (product): add trace_id propagation so billing can answer "why charged" queries. expose a header when fallback occurs.
Maya (eng-runtime): ops must get fallback_rate_{lane} and hedge_waste_pct. set alert: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained 10m.
Dan (orch): sounds good. I'll draft a minimal reconciler PR and proto tests.
Lea (sre): I'll add dashboards + runbook entries for fallbacks and hedging faults.
DeployBot: rollout queued: admission-proxy/minimal-surface -> staging at 2026-04-05T16:00:00Z.
Maya (eng-runtime): thanks team — keeping operator tiny should speed iterations while preserving cluster safety.
